Name: Matt Loomis
Badge: Layering Reading, Writing and Thinking
How does the Layering Reading, Writing, and Discussion approach compare to how you have previously supported students in engaging with multiple texts or teaching argument writing? How might this process shift or refine the way you guide students toward forming their own claims?:

This process is much more structured than what I typically have my students do in class, except when we are working on DBQs from Digital Inquiry Group, which typically have multiple primary and secondary source excerpts and predetermined sourcing, contextualization, and corroboration questions for students to answer. I feel like this process will allow me to create my own DBQs, and I can see using it at least once per unit in the future. This process will make writing claims more natural because of the diverse perspectives and emphasis on not forming an opinion before closely reading and reacting.

How would you describe the role of talk and discussion in your classroom right now? What kinds of opportunities do students have to rehearse ideas through conversation? What challenges have you encountered in making talk a meaningful part of the writing process?:
Discussion is very common and a key element of my classroom routines in Humanities, which is my honors level 8th Grade social studies course. In the regular track, students lack the foundation literacy necessary to consistently decode and comprehend texts independently, and they struggle with motivation and structured writing, so both the input and output are filled with challenges.
